title: Important Safety Instructions
text:
## Important Safety Instructions

**WARNING:**

TO REDUCE THE RISK OF FIRE OR ELECTRIC SHOCK, DO NOT EXPOSE THIS PRODUCT TO RAIN OR MOISTURE.

**CAUTION:**

TO REDUCE THE RISK OF ELECTRIC SHOCK, DO NOT REMOVE COVER (OR BACK). NO USER-SERVICEABLE PARTS INSIDE. REFER SERVICING TO QUALIFIED SERVICE PERSONNEL.

### Cleaning

Unplug this television receiver from the wall outlet before cleaning. Do not use liquid cleaners or aerosol cleaners. Use a damp cloth for cleaning. Do not use attachments not recommended by the television receiver manufacturer as they may cause hazards.

### Power Supply

This television receiver should be operated only from the type of power source indicated on the marking label. If you are not sure of the type of power supplied to your home, consult your television dealer or local power company.

### Installation

Do not use this television receiver near water, for example, near a bathtub, washbowl, kitchen sink or laundry tub, in a wet basement, or near a swimming pool, etc. Do not place this television receiver on an unstable cart, stand, or table. The television receiver may fall, causing serious injury to a child or an adult, and serious damage to the appliance. Use only with a cart or stand recommended by the manufacturer, or sold with the television receiver. Wall or shelf mounting should follow the manufacturer's instructions and should use a mounting kit approved by the manufacturer. Slots and openings in the cabinet and the back or bottom are provided for ventilation, and to insure reliable operation of the television receiver, and to protect it from overheating. These openings must not be blocked or covered. The openings should never be blocked by placing the television receiver on a bed, sofa, rug, or other similar surface. This television receiver should not be placed in a built-in installation such as a bookcase unless proper ventilation is provided. It is recommended not to operate this unit near speakers or big metallic furniture in order to keep their magnetism from disturbing color purity (uniformity) on the screen.

### Writing Model And Serial Numbers

The serial number and model number are found on the back of this unit. The serial number is unique to this unit. You should record requested information here and retain this guide as a permanent record of your purchase. Please retain your purchase receipt as your proof of purchase.

### Wet Location Marking

Apparatus shall not be exposed to dripping or splashing and no objects filled with liquids, such as vases, shall be placed on the apparatus.

### Use

Do not allow anything to rest on the power cord. Do not locate this television receiver where the cord will be abused by persons walking on it. Do not overload wall outlets and extension cords as this can result in fire or electric shock. Never push objects of any kind into this television receiver through cabinet slots as they may touch dangerous voltage points or short out parts that could result in a fire or electric shock. Never spill liquid of any kind on the television receiver.

### Service

Do not attempt to service this television yourself as opening or removing covers may expose you to dangerous voltage or other hazards. Refer all servicing to qualified personnel.

- Description of controls: 6

- Various functions: clock, timers, game mode, key lock, auto demonstration, favorite channels, and fine tuning.

Troubleshooting check list... 23

1. POWER BUTTON (or ON/OFF): Refer to "Turning on/off the TV".
2. NUMBER BUTTONS: To select the desired channel directly.
3. APC (Auto Picture Control) BUTTON: To adjust the factory preset pictures corresponding to the lighting around.
4. MENU BUTTON: To display on-screen menus.
5. CHANNEL UP/DOWN arrow BUTTONS:
  - To select the desired channel.
  - To select the desired menu item when menu is displayed on the screen.

  VOLUME UP/DOWN arrow BUTTONS:
  - To increase or decrease volume level.
  - To enter or adjust the selected menu when menu is displayed on the screen.

  ENTER(O) BUTTON:
  - To exit from the displayed menu.
  - To memorize the adjusted menu.
  - To recall the current TV mode (by remote control only).
6. FCR (Favorite Channel Review) BUTTON: To select the favorite channel. Refer to "Favorite channel memory".
7. AUTO PRG. (Auto program) BUTTON: To memorize channels by AUTO PROGRAM.
8. EYE/asterisk BUTTON (some models): To switch on or off eye picture. Refer to "Enjoying the Eye Function". Asterisk: No function.
9. REVIEW BUTTON (some models): To return to the previous channel.
10. WIDE/ZOOM/asterisk BUTTON (some models): To select the desired picture format (4:3, 16:9 or ZOOM). Asterisk: No function.
11. MUTE BUTTON: To mute the sound. Press again to restore the muted sound.
12. TV/VIDEO BUTTON: To select TV, VIDEO or COMPONENT mode.
13. CAPTION BUTTON (some models): To select the CAPTION mode. Refer to "Closed caption function".
14. SLEEP BUTTON: To set the desired sleep time.
15. MEMORY/ERASE BUTTON (some models): To memorize or erase the desired channel.
16. PICTURE BUTTON: To display picture modes one by one.

title: Turning on/off the TV
text:
## Turning on/off the TV

Press the POWER (or ON/OFF) button on the set. At this time, the set switches to standby mode and the standby indicator lights up in red. To switch the TV on from standby mode, press the TV/VIDEO, CH +/- button on the set or POWER, TV/VIDEO, CH +/- or NUMBER button on the remote control. A channel number will be displayed on the screen. The on-screen display will disappear after a few seconds. Press the POWER button on the remote control. It reverts to standby mode. To switch the TV off, press the POWER button on the set

1. Press the MENU button and then the right arrow button until the menu is displayed as shown right.

text:
## Memorizing Channels

This is the function to memorize all the active channels in your area before you can use the TV. There are two ways of memorizing channels. You can use either. One is called AUTO PROGRAM and the other is called MANUAL PROGRAM. In AUTO PROGRAM the TV will memorize the channels in ascending order. If there are additional channels you want to add or delete, you can manually add or delete those channels.

### Memorizing the Channels by AUTO PROGRAM

AUTO PROGRAM searches and memorizes all the active channels in your area then you can select the desired channel with the arrow buttons.

**Using the A.PROG button**

You can conveniently perform AUTO PROGRAM using the AUTO PRG. button on the remote control.

1. Press the AUTO PROG. button.
2. Press the right arrow or AUTO PROG. button. The AUTO PROGRAM starts now.

If you want to stop auto programming, press the ENTER button. Only the channels searched up to that time are memorized.


<PIC:Manual35_5>
{{image description: Simple on-screen prompt for auto programming, showing a highlighted Auto prog. button on the left and To start with a right arrow on the right.}}


Notes:
- If the programmed signal has poor quality, memorize again in the Auto prog.
- AUTO PROGRAM stores all receivable channels regardless of receiving signal (RF, Cable).
- If channels of general wireless TV and cable TV are duplicated, press the number buttons (0~9) to change channels.


<PIC:Manual35_6>
{{image description: Small diagram showing Channels of general wireless TV and Channels of Cable TV in two boxes connected by a two-way arrow.}}


<PIC:Manual35_7>
{{image description: Auto program progress screen. It reads Auto prog., shows TV 19, a progress bar at 5 percent, and a Stop option below.}}


**Using the MENU button**

1. Press the MENU button and then the right arrow button until the menu is displayed as shown right.
2. Press the down arrow and then the right arrow button to select Auto prog.
3. Press the arrow button to enter the Auto prog. mode
4. The AUTO PROGRAM starts now


<PIC:Manual35_8>
{{image description: Channel menu screen with Auto prog., Manual, and Favorite listed under a CH icon. The footer shows Move, Next, and Exit navigation hints.}}


### Memorizing the Channels by MANUAL PROGRAM

Using the MEMORY/ERASE button

You can conveniently perform MANUAL PROGRAM using the MEMORY/ERASE button on the remote control.

1. Press the arrow or NUMBER buttons to select the channel number you want to memorize or erase.
2. Press the MEMORY/ERASE button to select Memory or Erase. The on-screen display appears as shown right.


<PIC:Manual35_9>
{{image description: Channel menu screen with Manual highlighted. A right-side panel says To set. The footer shows Move, Next, and Back navigation hints.}}


**Using the MENU button**

1. Press the MENU button and then the right arrow button until the menu is displayed as shown right.
2. Press the right arrow and then use the up/down arrow button to select Manual
3. Press the right arrow button and then use the up/down arrow button to select Channel.
4. Press the right arrow button and then use the up/down arrow button to select the channel number you want to memorize or erase.


5. Press the right arrow button and then use the up/down arrow button to select Memory.
<PIC:Manual35_10>
{{image description: Small on-screen status box reading CATV 95 Memory on a gray television background.}}




6. Press the arrow button and then arrow button to select On or off.
7. Repeatedly press the MENU button to exit.

text:
## Closed caption function (some models)

Closed captioning is a process which converts the audio portion of a television program into written words, which then appear on the television screen in a form similar to subtitles. Closed captions allow viewers to read the dialogue and narration of television programs.

### Using Closed Captions

Captions are the subtitles of the dialogue and narration of television programs. For prerecorded programs, program dialogue can be arranged into captions in advance. It's possible to caption a live program by using a process called "real-time captioning", which creates captions instantly. Real-time captioning is normally done by professional reporters using a machine shorthand system and computer for translation into English. Captioning is an effective system for the hearing-impaired, and it can also aid in teaching language skills.
- The picture at left shows a typical caption


<PIC:Manual35_36>
{{image description: Closed-caption sample screen showing three cartoon animal faces above a black caption bar that reads FOLLOW ME.}}


### Caption Tips
- Not all TV broadcasts include closed caption signals
- Sometimes TV stations broadcast two different caption signals on the same channel. By selecting MODE 1 or MODE 2, you can choose which signal you view. MODE 1 is usually the signal with the captions, while MODE 2 might show demonstration or programming information.
- Your TV might not receive caption signals normally in the following situations.

1. Poor reception conditions are encountered:

- **IGNITION:**

Picture may flutter, drift, suffer from black spots or horizontal streaking. Usually caused by interference from automobile ignition systems, neon lamps, electrical drills and other electrical appliances.


<PIC:television0_01>
{{image description: Black-and-white example of poor television caption reception, showing a distorted face and horizontal broken caption-like streaks across the image.}}


- **GHOSTS:**

Ghosts are caused when the TV signal splits and follows two paths. One is the direct path and the other is reflected off tall buildings, hills or other objects. Changing the direction or position of the antenna may improve reception.


<PIC:television0_02>
{{image description: Black-and-white example image of a person with a hat and microphone, with blurred or ghosted areas around the figure.}}


- **SNOW:**

If your receiver is located at the weak, fringe area of a TV signal your picture may be marred by small dots. It may be necessary to install a special antenna to improve the picture.


2. An old, bad or illegally recorded tape is played.
3. Strong, random signals from a car or airplane interfere with the TV signal.
4. The signal from the antenna is weak.
5. The program wasn't captioned when it was produced, transmitted or taped
<PIC:television0_03>
{{image description: Black-and-white noisy reception example showing the same person with heavy speckling and distorted caption-like image noise.}}



**Using the Text Function**

Text services give a wide variety of information on all kind of subjects (ex. captioned program lists, weather forecasts, stock exchange topics, news for hearing-impaired) through the full TV screen. But not all stations offer text services, even though they might offer captioning.

Note: In the event you receive a poor signal, an empty black box may appear and disappear, even when the text mode is selected. This is normal function in such an event.

### Operating the Caption and Text

Using the CAPTION button
1. Press the CAPTION button
2. Press the CAPTION button to select OFF, Mode1, Mode2, Text1 or Text2.
3. Press the ENTER(O) button to exit


<PIC:Manual35_37>
{{image description: TV on-screen caption example with two rectangular selections labeled Caption and Mode1 on a gray screen.}}


**Using the MENU button**

1. Press the MENU button and then use arrow button to select the Special menu.
2. Press the down arrow and then the right arrow button to select Caption
3. Press the right arrow button and then use the up/down arrow button to select Off, Mode1, Mode2, Text1 or Text2.
4. Repeatedly press the MENU button to exit


<PIC:Manual35_38>
{{image description: TV settings menu screenshot with side icons and a list: Language, Input, Key lock, Caption, Game, and Auto demo. Caption is highlighted and a submenu shows Off, Mode1 selected, Text1, and Text2; bottom hints read Move, Next, and Back.}}


Note: This TV is programmed to remember the last mode used, even if you turn the TV off.

## Connection of external equipment (some models)

You can connect additional equipment, such as VCRs, camcorders etc. to your set. The jacks shown may be somewhat different from your set. These are an example drawing of typical jack layout.
1. IN 1 JACKS: Connect external equipment outputs (VCR, LASER DISC, CAMCORDER) to these inputs. Press the TV/VIDEO button to select VIDEO 1.
2. IN 2 JACKS: Connect external equipment outputs (VCR, LASER DISC, CAMCORDER) to these inputs. Press the TV/VIDEO button to select VIDEO 2 or S-VIDEO.
3. OUT JACKS: Connect external equipment inputs (VCR, Audio amplifier) to these outputs for recording or monitoring the selected program.
4. EARPHONE JACK (some models): In some models, this jack is located on the front or side of TV.

### Connecting AUDIO/VIDEO IN Jacks

1. Connect the audio/video output jacks of the VCR to IN 1(A/V) jacks on the side or back of TV. If you connect the audio jack only, you can't hear the sound from the TV.
2. Press the TV/VIDEO button to select VIDEO 1.

Note: In some stereo models, if you connect the audio/video output jacks of the VCR to the IN 2 (A/V) jacks on the front or side of TV, select VIDEO 2.
3. Press the PLAY button on the VCR. The video playback is on the TV screen


<PIC:Manual35_42>
{{image description: Playback VCR to TV connection diagram showing AV VIDEO, L(MONO), and AUDIO(R) cables connected from the VCR to the TV IN or AV IN 2 jacks.}}


Note: In case of MONO VCR, connect the output jack of VCR to the AUDIO L/MONO IN jack of TV so that the sound can be heard from both speakers. If you connect it to the AUDIO R IN jack of TV the sound is heard only from right speaker.

Note: In some mono models, when the input jacks on the front panel and back panel are connected to external equipments at the same time, the input jacks on the front panel have priority over the input jacks on the back panel of the TV.

### Connecting the S-VHS VCR (some models)

1. Connect the S-VHS output jack of the VCR to the S-VIDEO jack on the side or back of TV.
2. Connect the audio/video output jacks of the VCR to the IN 2(A/V) jacks on the front or side of TV.
3. Press the TV/VIDEO button to select S-VIDEO
4. Press the PLAY button on the VCR. The video playback is visible on the TV screen


<PIC:television0_04>
{{image description: Playback VCR connection diagram showing a cable from the VCR to the TV VIDEO input and AV IN 2 jacks on the TV side panel.}}


### VCR Recording (some models)

1. Connect the audio/video input jacks of the recording VCR to the OUT(A/V) jacks on the back.
2. Select the program number on the TV.
3. Set the recording VCR to record


<PIC:television0_05>
{{image description: Recording VCR connection diagram showing three AV cables from the TV OUT jacks to the recording VCR AV input jacks.}}

1. Connect the output jacks of the playback VCR to the IN 1(A/V) jacks on the side or back of TV.
2. Connect the input jacks of the recording VCR to the OUT (A/V) jacks on the back of TV.
3. Press the TV/VIDEO button to select VIDEO 1. If you connect it to the IN 2 (A/V) jacks on the side of TV, you should select VIDEO 2.

Simple on-screen prompt for auto programming, showing a highlighted Auto prog. button on the left and To start with a right arrow on the right.
Small diagram showing Channels of general wireless TV and Channels of Cable TV in two boxes connected by a two-way arrow.

Channel menu screen with Auto prog., Manual, and Favorite listed under a CH icon. The footer shows Move, Next, and Exit navigation hints.
Channel menu screen with Manual highlighted. A right-side panel says To set. The footer shows Move, Next, and Back navigation hints.
Small on-screen status box reading CATV 95 Memory on a gray television background.
Manual channel settings menu. The left pane lists Channel, Memory, and Fine, with Memory highlighted; the right pane shows On selected above Off. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Volume on-screen display showing Volume 15 with a horizontal bar partly filled.
Mute on-screen display with a centered gray box labeled Mute.
Timer menu screen listing Clock, Off timer, On timer, and Auto off. Clock is highlighted and the right pane shows --:-- AM. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Timer menu screen with Off timer highlighted. The right pane shows 11:40PM and Off. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Timer menu screen with On timer highlighted. The right pane shows 11:40PM, TV 6, Vol. 30, and Off. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Sleep timer on-screen display with a gray bar labeled Sleep and a placeholder value shown as ---.
Timer menu screen with Auto off highlighted. The right pane offers On and Off, with Off selected. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Setup menu screen with Game highlighted. The right pane says To start. The left list includes Language, Input, Key lock, Caption, Game, and Auto demo.
Setup menu with Key lock highlighted. The right pane shows On selected above Off. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Setup menu with Auto demo highlighted. The right pane says To start. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Channel favorite menu with Favorite highlighted. The right panel lists CATV 95 at the top followed by dashed empty entries. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Channel menu screen listing Auto prog., Manual, and Favorite, with footer controls Move, Next, and Exit.
Manual channel fine-tuning menu with Fine highlighted and value 0 shown in the right pane. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Magic eye picture adjustment display showing values Contrast 100, Brightness 60, Color 50, Sharpness 60, and Stop: EYE.
On-screen status message reading Magic eye off inside a gray rectangular box.
Auto picture control on-screen selector with APC highlighted and Clear shown as the selected picture mode.

Picture menu screen with APC highlighted. The list includes APC, Contrast, Brightness, Color, Sharpness, and Tint; the right pane lists Magic eye, Clear, Optimum, Soft, and User, with Magic eye selected.
Picture menu screen listing APC, Contrast, Brightness, Color, Sharpness, and Tint without a value panel filled in. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Picture menu screen with Contrast highlighted and value 100 shown beside a horizontal adjustment bar. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Sound menu screen with DASP highlighted. The right pane lists Flat, Music, Movie, Sports, and User, with Flat selected. The left list also includes AVL, Balance, Treble, and Bass.
Sound menu screen with AVL highlighted. The right pane offers On and Off, with Off selected. Footer shows Move, Next, and Back.
Sound menu screen with Balance highlighted and value 0 shown with a centered horizontal balance scale.
Sound menu screen with Treble highlighted and value 50 shown with a partially filled horizontal bar.
Sound menu screen with Bass highlighted and value 50 shown with a partially filled horizontal bar.
Closed-caption sample screen showing three cartoon animal faces above a black caption bar that reads FOLLOW ME.
Black-and-white example of poor television caption reception, showing a distorted face and horizontal broken caption-like streaks across the image.
Black-and-white example image of a person with a hat and microphone, with blurred or ghosted areas around the figure.
Black-and-white noisy reception example showing the same person with heavy speckling and distorted caption-like image noise.
TV on-screen caption example with two rectangular selections labeled Caption and Mode1 on a gray screen.

TV settings menu screenshot with side icons and a list: Language, Input, Key lock, Caption, Game, and Auto demo. Caption is highlighted and a submenu shows Off, Mode1 selected, Text1, and Text2; bottom hints read Move, Next, and Back.
Antenna connection diagram for Combination VHF/UHF Antennas showing 300 ohm flat wire, 300 to 75 ohm adapter, TV rear 75 ohm antenna jack, 75 ohm coaxial cable, and 75 ohm CATV cable.
Two-step antenna connection diagram: step 1 shows a 75 ohm antenna jack to a 300 to 75 ohm adapter; step 2 shows a 75 ohm CATV cable from cable TV source.
TV jack location diagram showing numbered connection panels with component/DVD inputs, OUT and IN AV video and audio jacks, earphone, and S-VIDEO jack labels for some models.
Playback VCR to TV connection diagram showing AV VIDEO, L(MONO), and AUDIO(R) cables connected from the VCR to the TV IN or AV IN 2 jacks.
Playback VCR connection diagram showing a cable from the VCR to the TV VIDEO input and AV IN 2 jacks on the TV side panel.
Recording VCR connection diagram showing three AV cables from the TV OUT jacks to the recording VCR AV input jacks.
Connection diagram showing a playback VCR connected to TV input jacks and a recording VCR connected to TV output jacks, with arrows indicating signal flow through the TV.
DVD to TV component connection diagram showing Y, Pb, Pr component cables and audio cables connected between the back panel of DVD and the TV connection panel.
Note table matching TV INPUT Y, Pb, Pr to DVD OUTPUT options Y/Cb/Cr, Y/B-Y/R-Y, Y/Pb/Pr, and Y/PB/PR.

TV troubleshooting chart matching symptoms to checks. Symptoms listed are No power, No picture or sound, Poor picture but good sound, Poor reception, Lines in picture, Ghosts (multiple images), Remote control does not work, and Cannot tune desired channel. The check list includes power cord plugged in, television turned on, remote batteries, trying another channel, antenna connections, local interference, antenna adjustment, picture control adjustment, and auto program channel setup.

Common poor reception conditions include ignition interference, ghosts, and snow. Ignition interference may cause the picture to flutter, drift, show black spots, or show horizontal streaks, and it is usually caused by automobile ignition systems, neon lamps, electrical drills, or other electrical appliances. Ghosts occur when a TV signal splits and follows two paths: a direct path and a reflected path from tall buildings, hills, or other objects. Snow can appear in weak fringe areas and may require a special antenna. The manual also notes random interference from cars or airplanes, weak antenna signals, poor-quality old tapes, and bad outdoor antennas or weathered antenna cables.
